discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in a5422b406b and 6f917322e1: `resolve_destination()` canonicalizes every existing ancestor, so a symlinked parent that points at the source is resolved before the comparison. `clone_first_worktree_rejects_destination_behind_a_symlinked_parent` covers it.

Fixed in 57b5e5bd4a: only a missing `omp-setup` counts as no mark; any other read error now fails `worktrees()` instead of reporting the setup as finished, so `pr_checkout` stops rather than reusing the worktree. Rust test: with the mark replaced by something unreadable (a directory), the listing fails; with errors swallowed as on the previous commit, it reports no owner.

Fixed in e3e670de4e: the rollback now removes the registration's `gitdir` first. If that fails, it touches nothing else, so the worktree stays listed with its live setup owner and other omp processes refuse it. Once `gitdir` is gone, neither git nor omp lists the worktree, so nothing can take it over, and the rest goes (`HEAD` next, then the directory, mark included). This also avoids an entry without `HEAD` that would make every listing fail. Rust tests (Unix): with `locked` impossible to remove, the rollback fails and the worktree is no longer listed while the listing still works; with the whole registration read-only, it stays listed with its owner.

Fixed in f43934c6d5: the rollback now only unlists the worktree once its checkout is gone (deleted, or already missing). If deleting the checkout fails, it leaves the registration and its setup mark untouched: the worktree stays listed and owned by this live process, so other omp processes refuse it, and `git worktree remove` can recover it, instead of leaving a directory whose `.git` points at deleted admin data. Rust test (Unix): with a read-only directory inside the checkout so it can't be deleted, the rollback fails and the worktree is still listed with its owner; on the previous commit it was no longer listed.
